react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites form a cohesive lipidmediator signature centred on arachidonic acid (AA) metabolism. Six of the seven compounds — arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-HETE (C04742), 5-HETE (C04805), 11,12,15-THETA (C14782), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) — are downstream products or alternative-pathway derivatives of AA, and they hit the same pathway cluster across three independent enrichment paradigms: RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 9.2×10⁻¹⁸, 6/6 shared hits), MetaboAnalystR PSEA (p=7.5×10⁻⁸, KEGG:hsa00590 rank-1), and Mummichog m/z-direct (p=5.0×10⁻⁴, rank-1, all 13 pathway members present in the input set). The 12/15-lipoxygenase products (15-HETE, 11,12,15-THETA) and the cycloxygenase-derived 15d-PGJ2 co-occur, suggesting simultaneous LOX and COX branch activation in the treatment condition. Leukotriene A4 confirms 5-lipoxygenase flux despite being the upstream parent of the LTC4 synthesis deficiency pathway that ranked first in RaMP. CDP (C00112) is a distinct signal mapping to pyrimidine metabolism / N-glycan biosynthesis, unrelated to the AA cluster. The convergence of three paradigms on KEGG:hsa00590 and MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism as the single dominant pathway, with five driver compounds all verified as pathway members by their presence in the MFN compound roster, establishes this as a robust multi-method finding.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on arachidonic acid-centered eicosanoid biosynthesis. MetaboAnalystR PSEA identified KEGG:hsa00590 (Polyunsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis) as the top-ranked pathway with p=7.5e-08, and that pathway contained five input metabolites: arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 11,12,15-THETA, 15-HETE, and 5-HETE. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis placed the MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism module at rank-1 with p=8.4e-04, with metabolites_hit showing six compounds including arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, and 5-HETE mapped to the arachidonic acid node of the human metabolic function network. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned the REACT:R-HSA-140180 (COX reactions) pathway at rank 8 with FDR=0.00101, with arachidonic acid as the sole mapped metabolite. CDP appeared as a distinct signal, mapping to MUMM:N-Glycan biosynthesis (rank 7, p=0.057) and MUMM:vitamin_b5_coa_biosynthesis_from_pantothenate (rank 9, p=0.057) in the m/z network, indicating its separation from the eicosanoid cluster. Arachidonic acid is the substrate driving enrichment across all three methods. Five of the six eicosanoid compounds (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE, 11,12,15-THETA) are verified pathway members in KEGG:hsa00590, and three of these (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE) are confirmed in MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism. The 15d-PGJ2 compound (C14717) was not recovered in any pathway hit at the significance threshold used.

Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis placed MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism at rank-1 with p=3.36e-04.
Mummichog placed MUMM:leukotriene_metabolism at rank-4 with p=0.0255.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a core arachidonic acid-centered eicosanoid signal. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned 15 SMPDB entries at the top (ranks 0–14) all sharing the same six metabolites — arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE, 11,12,15-THETA, and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 — with FDR=9.17e-18 and fold enrichment ~858. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis placed MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism at rank-1 (p=3.36e-04) with all 13 input-compound equivalents mapped to the arachidonic acid node of the human metabolic function network, including the five core eicosanoids plus 15d-PGJ2. MUMM:leukotriene_metabolism (rank-4, p=0.0255) captured arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, and 15-HETE. CDP mapped only to MUMM:n_glycan_biosynthesis (rank-6, p=0.053) and MUMM:vitamin_b5_coa_biosynthesis_from_pantothenate (rank-8), indicating it is biologically distinct from the eicosanoid cluster. Arachidonic acid is the shared substrate linking the HETE branch, the leukotriene branch (via 5-lipoxygenase on leukotriene A4), and the prostaglandin branch (via COX on 15d-PGJ2), placing it as the primary driver metabolite across all paradigms.

use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead
FELLA R subprocess errored at runtime (currently 'argument is of length zero' on every sub6b-v3 task — W9 D4 stretch target); skip the network/diffusion paradigm and rely on ORA + mummichog

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a core arachidonic acid-centered eicosanoid signal. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned 15 SMPDB entries at the top (ranks 0–14) all sharing the same six metabolites — arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE, 11,12,15-THETA, and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 — with FDR=9.17e-18 and fold enrichment ~858. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis placed MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism at rank-1 (p=3.36e-04) with all 13 input-compound equivalents mapped to the arachidonic acid node of the human metabolic function network, including the five core eicosanoids plus 15d-PGJ2. MUMM:leukotriene_metabolism (rank-4, p=0.0255) captured arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, and 15-HETE. CDP mapped only to MUMM:n_glycan_biosynthesis (rank-6, p=0.053) and MUMM:vitamin_b5_coa_biosynthesis_from_pantothenate (rank-8), indicating it is biologically distinct from the eicosanoid cluster. Arachidonic acid is the shared substrate linking the HETE branch, the leukotriene branch (via 5-lipoxygenase on leukotriene A4), and the prostaglandin branch (via COX on 15d-PGJ2), placing it as the primary driver metabolite across all paradigms.
